notes.meaning: God pronounces sorrow and judgment against Jerusalem, though she should have been the holy city. Instead of living out God's pure ways, she has stained herself with rebellion and mistreats the weak and needy. The name of the city is not spoken at first, showing how far she has fallen from her high calling.

Jerusalem refused to listen to God's voice through His messengers, and she would not learn from His discipline. Instead of trusting the LORD, she put her confidence in human alliances and turned away from the God who had drawn near to her. The root of all her outward wickedness was this quiet refusal to stay close to the LORD.

The civil rulers, who should have protected the innocent, behave like hungry predators. The royal princes hunt the helpless like roaring lions, and the judges tear their victims like starved wolves prowling at sunset. They are so greedy for unjust gain that they do not even leave leftovers for the next morning.

The spiritual leaders are just as corrupt as the princes and judges. The false prophets are reckless and untruthful, making up their own messages instead of speaking the true word of God. The priests treat holy things as ordinary and twist the law to excuse wrongdoing, corrupting the very worship they were chosen to guard.

The righteous LORD lives in the midst of Jerusalem, and He never does wrong. Every single morning He faithfully displays His truth and justice through His law and prophets, never missing a dawn. Yet the corrupt leaders and people feel no embarrassment or shame for their sins, ignoring the pure God who is right beside them.

God reminds Jerusalem of how He destroyed other wicked nations, tearing down their towers and leaving their streets empty of people. He brought these ruins to teach His own people to revere Him and receive correction so their city would be spared. Instead of learning this lesson, the people got up early and eagerly ran to commit more evil deeds.

God commands the faithful remnant to wait patiently for the day when He rises up to act in judgment. He has resolved to gather nations and kingdoms together so that His holy anger and burning jealousy can sweep away evil like a devouring fire. This terrible shaking of the world is designed to purge out sin and bring relief to those who trust Him.

After the refining judgment, the LORD promises to purify the lips and speech of the peoples. Their unclean talk of idolatry will be replaced by genuine prayer, calling together on the name of the LORD. They will serve Him side by side with one purpose, like oxen pulling evenly under the same yoke.

differ.view: This promise refers to an earthly thousand-year reign of Christ, during which the world may speak one shared, pure language such as Hebrew.
The pure speech is fulfilled through the gospel and the Holy Spirit, beginning at Pentecost, turning people from idols to sincere worship in the church.

notes.meaning: Even from distant lands beyond the rivers of Cush, God's scattered people and worshippers will return to honor Him. The nations will come bringing humble prayers and spiritual offerings to the Lord. God remembers His people no matter how far away they have been driven.

In that day of renewal, God's forgiven people will no longer be crushed by the shame of their past rebellions. The LORD will remove the arrogant hypocrites who boasted in the temple and took false pride in the holy mountain. True worship will be cleansed of human arrogance and self-righteousness.

God will leave a remnant in the land made up of humble, lowly, and meek people. Stripped of worldly pride and self-reliance, they find all their confidence in the character and help of the LORD. Knowing their own weakness teaches them to lean entirely on God's grace.

This preserved remnant of Israel will turn away from wickedness and deceit, speaking the truth with sincere and pure hearts. Like a well-tended flock of sheep, they will feed in peace and lie down to rest without fear of enemies or corrupt rulers. Holiness of life leads directly to inward rest and safety under God's care.

God calls His purified people, named here as Daughter of Zion and Daughter of Jerusalem, to burst into loud songs and deep celebration. The repetition of shouts, singing, and gladness shows that this joy is overflowing and heartfelt. Those who have been rescued by God's mercy have every reason to rejoice with their whole being.

The cause for this great rejoicing is that God has canceled the punishments due to their sins and driven back their enemies. The LORD Himself, the true King of Israel, dwells among them as their defender and shepherd. With their sins pardoned and God in their midst, they will never have to dread calamity or evil again.

In that day, comforting words will be spoken to the people: they are told not to fear and not to let their hands hang limp in despair. Fear paralyzes believers, making them weak and unable to serve, but God's promises restore their strength. His people can go about their work with courage because their future is secure.

The LORD dwells with His people as a mighty warrior who saves them from every threat and danger. He takes great delight in them, resting silently and peacefully in His love, and even rejoicing over them with shouts of glad singing. The great God of heaven finds deep satisfaction in loving and cherishing His redeemed children.

The LORD promises to bring home those who grieved while in exile because they could not join in the sacred annual feast days. Being cut off from God's public house of worship was their heaviest trial, and their captors mocked them for it. God notices the tears of those who long for His worship and pledges to wipe away their disgrace.

God will personally deal with and bring down every enemy that harmed His people. He will tenderly rescue the lame and gather the scattered who have no human power to help themselves. In every country where they were treated with contempt and mockery, He will replace their shame with honor and praise.

The LORD finishes His message with a sure promise to gather His people together and bring them safely home. They will see this wonderful rescue with their very own eyes, leaving no doubt that God has done it. The once-despised people will be celebrated and honored across the earth because the LORD has spoken.
